description:
The castle at Wąsowo began as a neo-Gothic villa built between 1870 and 1872 to a design by the Berlin architect Gustav Erdmann for the Berlin banker Richard Hardt. It was built next to the older 18th-century Sczaniecki palace, which stands on the same estate.

Around 1900, in connection with a planned visit by Emperor Wilhelm II to Wąsowo, the villa was rebuilt into a castle.

Today the estate, set in a park, operates as a four-star hotel with a restaurant, a spa area and an indoor pool, with breakfast included on the rate seen.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At ul. Parkowa 1 in Wąsowo, in the Kuślin municipality of Greater Poland, near Nowy Tomyśl; Booking lists free private parking.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €113/night for a 16 m² Double Room with one queen bed, a private bathroom and a flat-screen TV, with breakfast included on the non-refundable rate seen (pay online); taxes included. A rate with free cancellation was around €122.

**On-site:** An indoor swimming pool, a spa area, a restaurant and on-site parking, within the park of the estate.

**Good to know:** The rate seen is non-refundable, so check the free-cancellation option if your plans may change. The estate has several buildings, so ask the hotel which one your room is in.

**Combine with:** [Racot Palace](/castles/poland/racot-castle), another palace hotel in Greater Poland.
